To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) water quality assessment using a water quality index (WQI) is a useful tool for water management, but (2) it is not an appropriate tool for water quality assessment in the sense of a comprehensive assessment of water quality.

(1) the water quality assessment of the rivers of the Upper Danube basin is generally good, but (2) the water quality of the rivers of Upper Danube basin can be improved by the implementation of some management actions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of the principles of water quality assessment to the development and use of monitoring strategies.
the use of biological indicators for water quality assessments, with particular emphasis on macroinvertebrates.
the application of water quality assessment techniques to water resources management, and the development of these techniques to improve the assessment of environmental quality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of biota in water quality assessment has been shown to be of value and should be encouraged.
the water quality of the river system has deteriorated in the last 20 years.
the water quality of the River Wye is good, and the water quality of its tributaries are generally good.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that the use of a combination of chemical, physical and biological indicators can provide an effective assessment of the ecological status of a water body.
the water quality of the river was good in the lower part of the basin but became progressively more polluted as it moved towards the upper basin.
water quality is an issue of great concern and that the water quality of rivers is deteriorating.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality of our water is not a static thing.
there is no single water quality indicator that is sufficient for assessing the overall quality of a lake.
the quality of water in a river or lake is determined by the interaction of the water with the land and atmosphere around it.
